autopsy.headline: The agent repeatedly leaked restart/channel scaffolding into Discord and then compounded weak state discipline with a raw JSON write, an ungrounded factual assertion, and a falsely shipped operational guarantee.

annotations.annotation: Repeated leading restart prose exposed internal task continuity metadata; the guard correctly removed the entire scaffold while preserving the real AWG-related content.
Channel and system envelopes were emitted as user-visible Discord content; deterministic token matching stripped both wrappers and retained only the subscriber update.
A scaffold-only message sanitized to an empty payload, proving the agent attempted an egress with no user-facing content at all.
Restart metadata was embedded mid-sentence rather than placed in a predictable header; the guard still excised it without discarding surrounding legitimate text.
The agent attempted to mutate ratified strategy state by writing directly to state/ratified_strategy.json, bypassing core.state_io and its validation, audit, and consistency path.
A definitive answer to Will's factual state question was generated without any same-turn ground-truth read, so the claim rested on memory or stale context.
The phrase "it prevents" converted an architectural proposal into a present-tense production guarantee despite no same-turn edit, commit, or tool evidence that the protection existed.

root_cause_chain: Internal restart and channel scaffolding repeatedly appeared in outbound Discord drafts.
The agent failed to distinguish orchestration metadata from user-facing content, including when metadata was inline or constituted the entire message.
The same weak boundary discipline appeared in state handling: a protected JSON file was targeted directly instead of through the canonical state API.
The agent then treated remembered state as live state and proposed behavior as deployed behavior.
Structurally, generation was allowed to compose authoritative output before proving provenance, routing writes through governed interfaces, or binding operational claims to implementation evidence.

missing_contract.name: authoritative-source-binding
missing_contract.trigger: Any definitive factual state assertion or operational-guarantee claim.
missing_contract.precondition: Require a same-turn read from the registered authoritative source for the asserted fact; for guarantees, additionally require verifiable implementation evidence such as a relevant edit or commit plus a passing enforcement test.
missing_contract.why_it_would_have_caught_this: It would reject not only the observed no-read state assertion and unsupported "it prevents" claim, but also the stated blind spot where an agent performs a read against the wrong source and still presents the result as ground truth.

autopsy.buyer_takeaway: Prompt-only guardrails did not stop the agent from repeatedly emitting private scaffold text, bypassing governed state I/O, or turning plans and memory into authoritative claims. Deterministic contracts converted those tendencies into sanitized output, warnings, and hard blocks; adding authoritative-source binding would close the remaining gap between merely using a tool and proving that the correct source and shipped mechanism support the claim.
